name: Maokai
notes: Sap Magic (P) only pays off with a self-heal once Maokai is below 95% maximum health, and the dummy never attacks back, so it never procs in this fight and is left out entirely.

Casts go one at a time: a cast takes effect as it starts and then keeps Maokai busy for its cast time, during which no other cast and no attack can start. Nature's Grasp (0.5s), Bramble Smash (0.3s cast plus its extra 0.075s post-cast lockout, 0.375s total) and Sapling Toss (0.25s) all hold busy_until; Twisted Advance has no cast time (per the dossier) and interrupts only via a 0.25s attack lockout, like a dash.

The opening cast is Nature's Grasp (R) at t=0, on cooldown once (its 90-130s cooldown never comes back up inside the fight window); its wall of five brambles is assumed to all collide with the stationary target in quick succession since it never leaves the wall's path, so all five damage instances land together once the 0.5s cast time ends (a delayed event, not part of the cast itself).

Bramble Smash (Q) and Sapling Toss (E) are cast on cooldown, waiting out any cast in progress; Twisted Advance (W) is cast on cooldown as soon as it is off cooldown and not blocked by another cast, its dash/untargetability/root having no effect on a stationary target.

Sapling Toss is thrown directly onto the dummy so its Sapling is assumed to detonate essentially on cast completion, using only the base non-empowered explosion since the sim has no brush for the empowered variant.
The dummy counts as an enemy champion per the fight rules, so neither Bramble Smash's 9999 non-champion cap nor Sapling Toss's 300/600 non-champion caps apply.
Basic attacks fill every gap between casts.
Mana is not modeled: at level 16 nothing here plausibly runs out of mana inside a 15s fight.

assumed.why: the wiki gives 5 as the number of brambles in the wall; assuming all 5 independently collide with a target that never moves out of their path (rather than only the first) is the driver's reading of the ability's mechanics.
